The crescent moon is the symbol of the Islamic calendar, which determines the start and end of the Islamic year. This name also may evoke thoughts and feelings of the tranquility and serenity often associated with the night sky, themes deeply rooted in Islamic art and poetry.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Islamic tradition, the moon plays a significant role in various spiritual practices. The phases of the moon serve as reminders of the passage of time, and as such, signify areas for reflection and personal growth. The moon also represents the divine guidance and the power of Allah, which is seen in how it provides light in the darkness. The name Sumiya, derived from the word for moon, carries these spiritual connotations, providing a constant reminder of the guidance and presence of Allah.
